nodes.name: Solvothermal MOF formation
nodes.procedure: 1 mmol equal of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (99%), Co(NO3)2·6H2O (99%), Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (99%), Cu(NO3)2·3H2O (99%), Mn(NO3)2·4H2O (99%), along with 10 mmol of benzene dicarboxylic acid and 3 mL of MXene suspensions, were combined in 40 mL of methanol. The mixture was stirred for 24 hours at 60°C to obtain MHE-MOFs.
nodes.source_text: 1 mmol equal of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (99%)... The mixture was stirred for 24 hours at 60°C to obtain MHE-MOFs.

nodes.name: Calcination of MHE-MOFs
nodes.procedure: The resulting MHE-MOFs sample was rinsed several times with deionized water to remove excess solution. Finally, the MHE-MOFs were heated to 500°C in a tube furnace in the air to obtain MHEO.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows dominant diffraction peaks at 30.2°, 35.6°, 43.3°, and 62.9° corresponding to (220), (311), (400), and (440) facets of cubic γ-Fe₂O₃ structure (JCPDS#39-1346) without obvious impurities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A series of dominant diffraction peaks at 30.2, 35.6, 43.3, and 62.9° are observed, in agreement with the (220), (311), (400), and (440) facets of cubic γ-Fe₂O₃ structure (JCPDS#39–1346) without obvious impurities...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms the content of each element in HEO is close to that of the precursor (MHE-MOFs), listed in Table S1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The composition of HEO was determined using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES), and the results are listed in Table S1... The content of each element in MHEO is close to that of the precursor (MHE-MOFs).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Eg vibration mode of MXene at 317.4 cm⁻¹, Ni(III)-O bending at 476.5 cm⁻¹, Fe(III)-O at 681.5 cm⁻¹, confirming successful MXene coupling and high valence metal states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak at 317.4 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to the Eg vibration mode of the MXene functional group; the peak at 476.5 cm⁻¹ corresponds to the bending vibration of Ni(III)-O bonds; while 681.5 cm⁻¹ corresponds to Fe(III)-O bonds...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows high-density discrete HEO nanoparticles uniformly loaded on MXene layers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Morphologies and structures of the MHEO were characterized with scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). As demonstrated in Fig. 1b-c and S6-S7, high-density and discrete HEO nanoparticles...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows HEO nanoparticles with diameters of 34.3 nm and 25.9 nm, average particle size 75.6 nm; HRTEM reveals polycrystalline phase with d-spacings of 2.46 Å (311) and 2.42 Å (222).
nodes.evidence_snippet: high-density and discrete HEO nanoparticles (One has a diameter of 34.3 nm, the other 25.9 nm) are uniformly loaded on MXene layers. The article size distribution of the MHEO is shown in Fig. S8, and the average size is 75.6 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM and SAED confirm polycrystalline HEO nanoparticles indexed to (440), (400), (311), (222) facets with d-spacings 2.46 Å (311) and 2.42 Å (222), slightly deviated from γ-Fe₂O₃ reference due to lattice distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM image (Fig. 1d) and the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Fig. 1f) reveal that those nanoparticles are the polycrystalline phase, mainly indexed to (440), (400), (311) and (222), corresponding to the d-spacings of 2.46 Å for (311) and 2.42 Å for (222), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms presence of Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Mn, Ti, O; high oxidation states with Fe 2p 710.45 eV (Fe³⁺), Co 2p 780.16 eV (Co³⁺)/783.24 eV (Co²⁺), Ni 2p 854.88 eV (Ni³⁺), Cu 2p 933.75 eV (Cu²⁺), Mn 2p 641.54/648.71 eV (Mn³⁺) and 644.89/653.03 eV (Mn⁴⁺); O 1s 531.5 eV indicates oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS survey spectrum of MHEO verifies the presence of Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Mn, Ti, and O... dominant peaks in the Fe 2p spectrum can be deconvoluted into two subpeaks at 710.45 (Fe³⁺) and 718.82 eV (Sat.)... all catalysts exhibit a peak at 531.5 eV corresponding to oxygen vacancies (Ov).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows strongest peak at g-factor 2.00 for HEO, indicating highest oxygen vacancy concentration compared to other samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the HEO sample exhibits the strongest peak at a g-factor of 2.00, demonstrating the highest level of oxygen vacancies in the HEO compared with other counterparts.

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS shows MHEO has markedly increased OH⁻ signals and higher concentrations of O⁻, OH⁻, OOH⁻ than HEO; lower Cl⁻ and ClOₓ⁻ penetration in MHEO due to MXene repulsion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the MHEO catalyst exhibits markedly increased signals of oxygen-containing intermediates, i.e., O⁻, OH⁻, and OOH⁻... MHEO exhibits lower levels of Cl⁻ and ClOₓ⁻ signals...

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR verifies presence of ClO⁻ groups and M-Cl vibrations at 424 and 880 cm⁻¹ only in HEO after stability test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) also verifies this conclusion well (Fig. 4b), vibrations of ClO- groups and M-Cl molecules are observed at 424 and 880 cm⁻¹ only in the HEO.
